questions.passage: Our surveys also indicated the more home damage they had incurred, the more likely it was that they had lost a loved one. This human loss could also have a lingering negative effect on well-being. So, we examined housing damage simultaneously with human losses. To consider each contribution to well-being while accounting for the other.
To prove that bereavement was harmless.
To replace survey reports with randomized disasters.

证明失亲无害。
以随机灾害替代问卷。

C lingering negative effect相反。

questions.passage: Solnit concludes: “Surrounding them [the wounded, killed, orphaned], often in the same city or even neighborhood, is a periphery of many more who are largely undamaged but profoundly disrupted—and it is the disruptive power of disaster that matters here, the ability of disasters to topple old orders and open new possibilities…. The very depth of emotion, the connecting to the core of one’s being, the calling into play one’s strongest feelings and abilities, can be rich, even on deathbeds, in wars and emergencies.”
questions.prompt: What possibility does Solnit emphasize in this quotation?
options: Disasters leave every person physically undamaged.
Disaster can disrupt old orders and call forth deep feelings and capacities.
All emergencies guarantee happiness.
Only directly injured people experience disruption.
optionsZh: 每个人身体都无损。
灾难可打破旧秩序，唤起深层情感能力。
所有紧急状况保证幸福。
只有直接受伤者受扰乱。
analyses: A wounded/killed/orphaned承认严重伤害。
B disruptive power/new possibilities和calling into play串联核心。
C can be rich不等于guarantee happiness。
D periphery...largely undamaged...profoundly disrupted指旁及人群。这里是著作引语的观点，不是实验概率估计。

evidence.quote: the ability of disasters to topple old orders and open new possibilities

vocabulary.context: 形容旧社会秩序被扰动的比喻

questions.translation: Solnit总结：伤者、死者、失孤者周围，同城甚至同社区还有更多大体无损却深受扰动者。关键是灾难打破旧秩序、开启新可能的扰动力量。情感深度、触及存在核心、调动最强情绪和能力，即使在病榻、战争和紧急状况中，也可能丰富。
